title: Cavity models of non-Abelian gauge theories
authors: Lucia Valor, Jacquelin Luneau, Klaus Liegener, Stefan Filipp, Peter Rabl
abstract: In quantum optics and related fields, cavity quantum electrodynamics provides a powerful framework for modeling the low-energy properties of bound charges coupled to electromagnetic fields, using a minimal set of atomic levels and isolated photonic modes. Here, we develop a similar framework for non-Abelian gauge theories, focusing on the pure-gauge dynamics of SU(2) fields as the conceptually simplest example. Starting from the corresponding Yang-Mills Lagrangian, we derive an SU(2) cavity Hamiltonian in the Coulomb gauge, represented in terms of only three localized bosonic modes. Unlike its non-interacting electromagnetic counterpart, this model exhibits a nontrivial excitation spectrum featuring bound composite gauge particles ('glueballs') as the lowest-energy configurations. We extend this framework to one-dimensional arrays of coupled SU(2) cavities and discuss the driven excitation of a glueball condensate and the clustering of multi-glueball states as two elementary interaction-induced processes in these models. These examples offer a glimpse into the multitude of novel many-body phenomena that arise within this cavity SU(2) framework and we show how this physics at the interface between particle physics and quantum optics can be experimentally explored using state-of-the-art superconducting quantum circuits.
summary: This paper adapts the powerful framework of cavity quantum electrodynamics to model non-Abelian gauge theories, using SU(2) as the simplest example. By deriving a minimal cavity Hamiltonian, the authors predict the existence of bound composite particles called 'glueballs' within this quantum optical setting. This work is significant because it proposes an experimental route to study fundamental particle physics phenomena using superconducting quantum circuits.
main_problem: The paper develops a framework to model the dynamics of non-Abelian gauge theories, specifically SU(2), using the established methodology of cavity quantum electrodynamics (Cavity QED).
main_result: The authors derive a minimal cavity SU(2) Hamiltonian involving three coupled bosonic modes, demonstrating that the model predicts novel phenomena like bound composite gauge particles ('glueballs') and condensate formation.
method: The approach involves quantizing the Yang-Mills Lagrangian in the Coulomb gauge and restricting the dynamics to a single-mode approximation, analogous to cavity QED.
model_or_system: The system is the pure-gauge dynamics of SU(2) fields, whose Hamiltonian is derived from the Yang-Mills Lagrangian. It is modeled using a cavity Hamiltonian expressed in terms of three localized bosonic modes, allowing for the application of quantum optics techniques.
key_observables: Bound composite gauge particles ('glueballs'), glueball condensate excitation, and multi-glueball state clustering.
important_parameters: The coupling constant 'g', the single-mode approximation limit, and the interaction strengths derived from the Yang-Mills structure.
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions include working in the Coulomb gauge, restricting the dynamics to the single-mode limit, and focusing initially on pure-gauge dynamics while neglecting matter fields.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the gauge fields described by the Yang-Mills Lagrangian, showing the localized mode function representation for the reduced cavity Hamiltonian.
paper_structure: The paper moves from the general Yang-Mills Lagrangian to the Hamiltonian density, applies canonical quantization in the Coulomb gauge, derives the single-mode cavity Hamiltonian, and finally extends the analysis to 1D arrays to study condensate formation.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges high-energy particle physics (non-Abelian gauge theories) with the controlled, experimentally accessible physics of cavity QED, suggesting a concrete pathway for quantum simulation.

The resulting reduced cavity Hamiltonian Hcav describes three interacting bosonic modes with annihilation (creation) operators ai (a† i) and supports different types of bound and excited glueball states that are analyzed in this work. Each site hosts three interacting gauge-boson modes with local interaction strength U, while neighboring cavities are coupled by single- boson hopping with amplitude J. In the regime of strong interactions, U ≫J, the low-energy excitations are local glueballs, represented schematically by two photons symmet- rically distributed among the three modes.
